Our north star

Opportunity and dignity must grow together.

The Trust's legal objects span education, healthcare, care homes, livelihoods and community welfare. Our strategy brings them together through one clear idea: build ability, protect dignity and strengthen responsibility.

M

Mission

To make meaningful skill development accessible to every learner we serve; connect education with capability and livelihood; and extend timely, dignified support to children, youth, elders, orphans, persons with disabilities and families facing medical or social hardship.

V

Vision

A skilled, responsible and compassionate India where quality education creates self-reliance, communities care for their most vulnerable members, and no person is left without dignity, guidance or an opportunity to progress.

Chapter 01 / 03
01 · Learn

Education that becomes capability.

Our 100% skill-development ambition goes beyond certificates. We aim to help learners build practical ability, confidence, work readiness, ethical judgment and lifelong learning habits.

02 · Care

Support that protects dignity.

Children, orphans, youth, elders, persons with disabilities and families facing medical emergencies need more than sympathy. They need timely assessment, responsible support and sustained follow-through.

03 · Contribute

Citizenship that strengthens society.

Skills reach their highest purpose when they are used responsibly. We want education, livelihood, inclusion, environmental care and community service to reinforce one another.

Programme framework

One trust. Seven connected fields of action.

These focus areas translate the registered charitable objects into a clear programme structure. Individual projects begin according to verified need, resources, partnerships and statutory requirements.

Education

Skills & learning

Schools, colleges, vocational centres, digital learning, libraries, research and support for learners in need.

Care

Children & youth

Child welfare, pre-school support, drop-out education, street-child services, sports, yoga and constructive youth engagement.

Dignity

Elders & orphans

Care-centre pathways, nutrition, shelter, companionship and appropriate health support for young and elderly people without dependable care.

Health

Medical support

Need-based medical aid, dispensary and medicine support, health camps, blood donation and emergency assistance partnerships.

Inclusion

Women & different abilities

Education, counselling, assistive devices, vocational preparation, self-employment and socio-economic advancement.

Livelihood

Rural & agricultural development

Youth self-employment, natural farming, livestock, small and cottage industries, market access and applied agri-training.

Our public charter

Purpose protected by the Trust Deed.

JOY Social Welfare Trust was constituted as a public charitable trust in 2026. The deed places public benefit, responsible management and charitable use of funds at the centre of its work.

Future direction

From individual support to lasting institutions.

Our long-term goal is to build infrastructure that continues serving society across generations.

01

Multiple educational institutions

A network of schools, colleges, polytechnics, vocational centres, libraries, laboratories and research facilities that unite strong academics with real-world skills.

02

Our own quality-focused syllabus

A learner-centred curriculum combining academic foundations, practical skills, digital fluency, ethics, health, civic responsibility and employability.

03

Multi-specialty service hospital

A professionally governed charitable-care model designed to improve access to appropriate medical support and emergency-response pathways.

04

Children and elder care centres

Safe, dignified environments integrating nutrition, healthcare, learning, protection, companionship and pathways towards independence.
